description: Trend Detective is a team for the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge (Lucknow). Lead: Sujal Giri, a student at the Indian Institute of Technology Patna. Our challenge is 'Be An Earth System Trend Detective!'. We are open to new members joining the team.
summary: Trend Detective tests 44 years of NASA climate data for Indian cities and answers one question: is the change real, or just noise? Pick a city and a variable — temperature or rainfall — and the dashboard fetches live data from the NASA POWER API, draws the annual trend, and runs a proper significance test (least-squares trend + t-test, p < 0.05). The verdict is shown in plain English, with the numbers beside it. Findings for Prayagraj, 1981–2024: temperature −0.08 °C per decade (R² = 0.034, t = −1.22) — not significant; rainfall +0.095 mm/day per decade (R² = 0.058, t = +1.61) — not significant. Across 8 Indian cities, temperature is significant in only 2 (Mumbai, Chennai — both coastal) while rainfall is significant in 5 of 8. Method: monthly values (1981–2024) from the NASA POWER API, averaged into annual means, least-squares trend line, two-tailed t-test on the slope (df = 42). No API key needed. Limitation: this is one MERRA-2 reanalysis grid point (0.5°), not a ground thermometer; local factors can mask a regional trend.
